title: What Do They Get When You Gift Storyworth?
summary: There is something to give on the day. You choose when the questions start. How gifting Storyworth works, and how to make the first week count.
body_markdown:
Storyworth is a year of weekly questions with a hardcover book at the end, which raises a fair question if you are buying it for the holidays in December. What do they unwrap on Christmas morning when the book won't be finished for a year?


It's a common hesitation about giving Storyworth or another storytelling servce as a present, and it is better answered before you buy than discovered on the day.


## **There is something to open**


You are not handing someone a receipt. Storyworth gives you a beautifully designed gift card to print and give to them on the day, so there's something for them to open. They'll also receive an emailed gift message with more information and instructions to get started. You can personalize and schedule that message when you purchase your Storyworth plan.


For a lot of families that moment turns out to be the gift. Explaining what it is, and letting them know you're interested in learning more about them and preserving their stories for generations, is the part they'll remember. The book that turns up a year later is the second gift.


## **They don't have to start right away**


Their first question will arrive by email or text on the first Monday after their gift message hits their inbox. If they need a little more time to get started you can pause their account or adjust their question frequency. It's their story to tell at their pace.


## **Help them get off to a great start**


Storytellers who stall tend to stall at the first question, not the fortieth. Three small things make that week go better.


Choose questions that feel relevant to their life. Think about the stories they already love to tell and the questions you've always wanted to ask. You can also front load their questions with ones that feel easy to answer so they have a chance to get into the habit of reflecting and sharing.


Make sure they know you're genuinely interested in knowing more about them and their life, and assure them that they don't need to provide long answers for every question. Even a few short sentences can mean a lot.


## **Nothing has to be set up**


There is no app to install and no account for them to create before they can start. A question arrives by email or text and they reply to it the way they reply to anyone.


If they would rather talk than type, they can answer by phone, including from a landline in three different ways. That matters for a parent who does not own a smartphone and is not about to start now.


## **You can bring in the rest of the family**


Family members can be added to the account to read stories as they are written, respond to them, and add memories of their own. They can also join your storyteller on a Family Call so they can ask questions and share memories together. This turns the gift from a private exchange into something everyone is part of.


If you are giving this at Christmas with everyone in the room, that is the thing to set up while you are all together.


## **Buying late is fine**


Nothing has to ship for the gift to work right away. The gift card you print is the thing you give, and the questions start the next Monday morning.


Completing the book takes around a year but the gift itself is ready the moment you buy it. That means you can purchase a Storyworth plan for someone you love right up until Christmas morning.


## What to check if you are comparing services


Most guided memoir services are sold as presents, and they handle the giving partdifferently. Remento, Memorygram, StoryTerrace, Storii, My Life in a Book, Meminto, MyStories and Memowrite each make their own assumptions about how a gift reaches somebody.


Three questions are worth asking of any of them:


1. **Is there something to give on the day?** A service that only sends an email to the storyteller leaves you with nothing to hand over.
2. **Can family be involved?** A truly meaningful gift brings the whole family together to share memories together.
3. **Does the storyteller need to be tech savvy?** Can they use tech they're already comfortable with like a phone call or email?
